AgentOrchestratorNode.description: The agentOrchestrator node is a specialized agentLoop used for orchestrating multi-agent hand-offs to achieve a specified goal. It includes system prompts specialized to enable identifying the correct agent from a pool of available agents and routing tasks to the identified agents. The node may loop (up to maxLoops) to perform multiple hand-offs until the goal is achieved or the loop limit is reached.

A2ASendResponseNode.description:
This node is used to generate the response for an a2aOnMessage execution. The response will ALWAYS be a Task object as defined in the A2A specification.

This node doesn't define the entire Task object but only the status, artifacts and metadata fields. The id, contextId and history are automatically populated by the trigger.NOTE: Notice that this node doesn't specify a connection, since it operates on the context already defined by the a2a_onMessage trigger

GenerateNode.description: The *generate* node calls an LLM to generate text. It makes a single call to the LLM without tools and without looping. Use this node when the flow requires a one-shot LLM invocation for content generation (e.g. summarization, templated text, etc) with no tool use or iterative agent behavior.

MCPCallToolNode.description: The mcp_callTool node is used to explicitly invoke an MCP tool. The call doesn't occur as a decision from an agent node but as a deterministic step defined by the graph author.

MCPCallToolNodeProperties.description: Properties for the MCP CallTool node that explicitly invokes an MCP tool as a deterministic step.

connection.description: A reference to an MCP connection

toolName.description: The name of the tool to call

arguments.description: The tool's input arguments. Can be skipped if the tool takes no arguments

headers.description: Headers to be added when sending requests to the MCP server. Useful for use cases such as authorization, correlation, etc

HttpHeaders.description: HTTP headers as key-value pairs. Keys must be valid HTTP header names.

LLMRef.description: A reference to an LLM Provider

A2ASendMessageNode.description: The primary operation for initiating interactions with external A2A agents. Clients send a message to an agent and receive either a task that tracks the processing or a direct response message.

AgentCard.description:
The AgentCard is a self-describing manifest for an agent. It provides essential
metadata including the agent's identity, capabilities, skills, supported
communication methods, and security requirements.

additionalInterfaces.description:
A list of additional supported interfaces (transport and URL combinations).
This allows agents to expose multiple transports, potentially at different URLs.

Best practices:
- SHOULD include all supported transports for completeness
- SHOULD include an entry matching the main 'url' and 'preferredTransport'
- MAY reuse URLs if multiple transports are available at the same endpoint
- MUST accurately declare the transport available at each URL

Clients can select any interface from this list based on their transport capabilities
and preferences. This enables transport negotiation and fallback scenarios.

capabilities.description: A declaration of optional capabilities supported by the agent.

defaultInputModes.description:
Default set of supported input MIME types for all skills, which can be
overridden on a per-skill basis.

defaultOutputModes.description:
Default set of supported output MIME types for all skills, which can be
overridden on a per-skill basis.

description.description:
A human-readable description of the agent, assisting users and other agents
in understanding its purpose.
examples: Agent that helps users with recipes and cooking.

documentationUrl.description: An optional URL to the agent's documentation.

iconUrl.description: An optional URL to an icon for the agent.

name.description: A human-readable name for the agent.

preferredTransport.description:
The transport protocol for the preferred endpoint (the main 'url' field).
If not specified, defaults to 'JSONRPC'.

IMPORTANT: The transport specified here MUST be available at the main 'url'.
This creates a binding between the main URL and its supported transport protocol.
Clients should prefer this transport and URL combination when both are supported.

protocolVersion.description: The version of the A2A protocol this agent supports.

provider.description: Information about the agent's service provider.

security.description:
A list of security requirement objects that apply to all agent interactions. Each object
lists security schemes that can be used. Follows the OpenAPI 3.0 Security Requirement Object.
This list can be seen as an OR of ANDs. Each object in the list describes one possible
set of security requirements that must be present on a request. This allows specifying,
for example, "callers must either use OAuth OR an API Key AND mTLS."

securitySchemes.description:
A declaration of the security schemes available to authorize requests. The key is the
scheme name. Follows the OpenAPI 3.0 Security Scheme Object.

signatures.description: JSON Web Signatures computed for this AgentCard.

skills.description: The set of skills, or distinct capabilities, that the agent can perform.

supportsAuthenticatedExtendedCard.description:
If true, the agent can provide an extended agent card with additional details
to authenticated users. Defaults to false.

url.description:
The preferred endpoint URL for interacting with the agent.
This URL MUST support the transport specified by 'preferredTransport'.

version.description: The agent's own version number. The format is defined by the provider.

AgentLoopNode.description:
The reasoning node invokes an agent either by definition or by reference, enabling reuse of LLM-powered logic, toolchains, or full graphs from elsewhere in the specification. The reasoning node may accept parameters that define which agent, what prompt or context to use, tool selection, responses, and where to continue after invocation.

The reasoning node can take two shapes: a reference object or a full definition.

IfNode.description: The if node provides branching logic within a graph, allowing dynamic routing of control flow based on the evaluation of one or more conditions. Each if node contains a conditions array, where each item specifies a when expression and a corresponding to target. The if evaluates conditions in the order listed: the first branch whose when evaluates to true is selected and its to target is followed. If none match, the default action is to jump to the to node specified at the top level of the if. When expressions use the same expression language as other graph nodes, e.g., {{variables.value > 5}}. The first matching when's to will be taken; further branches are ignored. A branch with no when acts as the default/else branch.

protocolVersion.description: The version of the protocol being used. This is used to determine the structure and capabilities of the data.

transport.description: The transport protocol used for communication. This defines how the data is transmitted between the client and server.

provider.description: The service provider of the MCP server.

logging.description: Present if the server supports sending log messages to the client.

resources.description: A list of resources available in the mcp api. Each resource has a URI, name, description, MIME type, and annotations that provide additional metadata.

resourceTemplates.description: A list of resources available in the mcp api. Each resource has a URI, name, description, MIME type, and annotations that provide additional metadata.

prompts.description: A list of prompts available in the mcp api. Each prompt has a name, description, and arguments that define the expected input format for the prompt.

platform.description: The platform the mcp server is running

securitySchemes.description: Security scheme details used for authenticating with this agent.

SetVariablesNode.description: Assigns a value to the specified variable. If the variable is undefined, it is instantiated with the provided value. If the variable already exists, its current value MUST be overwritten.

A2ASendStreamNode.description:
The a2aSendStream node behaves similarly to a2aSendMessage, but enables real-time streaming of updates throughout message processing, as described in the A2A specification.

This node accepts the same input parameters as a2aSendMessage. However, its output ports and event transitions are specialized for handling real-time streaming events:

UnSetVariablesNode.description: Removes a specific variable from the graph's variable store. No action is taken if the variable is undefined or has already been removed

ServerCapabilities.description: Capabilities that a server may support. Known capabilities are defined here, in this schema, but this is not a closed set: any server can define its own, additional capabilities.

AgentSkill.description: Represents a distinct capability or function that an agent can perform.

description.description:
A detailed description of the skill, intended to help clients or users
understand its purpose and functionality.

examples.description:
Example prompts or scenarios that this skill can handle. Provides a hint to
the client on how to use the skill.
examples: I need a recipe for bread

id.description: A unique identifier for the agent's skill.

inputModes.description: The set of supported input MIME types for this skill, overriding the agent's defaults.

name.description: A human-readable name for the skill.

outputModes.description: The set of supported output MIME types for this skill, overriding the agent's defaults.

security.description:
Security schemes necessary for the agent to leverage this skill.
As in the overall AgentCard.security, this list represents a logical OR of security
requirement objects. Each object is a set of security schemes that must be used together
(a logical AND).

tags.description: A set of keywords describing the skill's capabilities.

name.description: The name of the variable to set

configuration.description: An optional object specifying additional instructions, preferences, or runtime configuration parameters for how this send-message request should be processed by the recipient agent and the A2A backbone. This could influence output modes, push notification preferences, history limits, blocking behavior, and more.

message.description: The main content of the send-message operation. This is a Message object (see Message for full specification), and it must contain all required message fields as described in the A2A protocol: a unique ID, sender role, message parts, and any associated metadata or extensions.

tenant.description: An optional tenant identifier. This string may be used in multi-tenant platforms or environments to explicitly specify which tenant context this message should operate under. If provided, it is typically appended as a path parameter within API endpoints to route the request.

metadata.description: A flexible key-value map (object) that allows for arbitrary additional information, context, or custom properties to be included alongside the send-message request. Clients and platforms may use this to supply implementation-specific context, correlation identifiers, feature hints, or custom operation flags.

Declares a combination of a target URL and a transport protocol for interacting with the agent.
This allows agents to expose the same functionality over multiple transport mechanisms.

_meta.description: See [General fields: `_meta`](/specification/2025-06-18/basic/index#meta) for notes on `_meta` usage.

description.description:
A description of what this template is for.

This can be used by clients to improve the LLM's understanding of available resources. It can be thought of like a "hint" to the model.

mimeType.description: The MIME type for all resources that match this template. This should only be included if all resources matching this template have the same type.

icons.description:
Optional set of sized icons that the client can display in a user interface.

Clients that support rendering icons MUST support at least the following MIME types:
- `image/png` - PNG images (safe, universal compatibility)
- `image/jpeg` (and `image/jpg`) - JPEG images (safe, universal compatibility)

Clients that support rendering icons SHOULD also support:
- `image/svg+xml` - SVG images (scalable but requires security precautions)
- `image/webp` - WebP images (modern, efficient format)

If not provided, the name should be used for display (except for Tool,
where `annotations.title` should be given precedence over using `name`,

This object specifies the type of trigger, the connection details (defined inline), relevant policies, method filters, and a file reference to the A2A card definition.

Defines a security scheme that can be used to secure an agent's endpoints.
This is a discriminated union type based on the OpenAPI 3.0 Security Scheme Object.

configuration.description: An optional object specifying additional instructions, preferences, or runtime configuration parameters for how this send-message request should be processed by the recipient agent and the A2A backbone. This could influence output modes, push notification preferences, history limits, blocking behavior, and more.

message.description: The main content of the send-message operation. This is a Message object (see Message for full specification), and it must contain all required message fields as described in the A2A protocol: a unique ID, sender role, message parts, and any associated metadata or extensions.

Clients and platforms may use this to supply implementation-specific context, correlation identifiers, feature hints, or custom operation flags.

MutualTLSSecurityScheme.description: Defines a security scheme using mTLS authentication.

description.description: An optional description for the security scheme.

type.description: The type of the security scheme. Must be 'mutualTLS'.

taskSupport.description:
Indicates whether this tool supports task-augmented execution.
This allows clients to handle long-running operations through polling
the task system.

- "forbidden": Tool does not support task-augmented execution (default when absent)
- "optional": Tool may support task-augmented execution
- "required": Tool requires task-augmented execution

Default: "forbidden"

required.description: Whether this argument must be provided.

title.description:
Intended for UI and end-user contexts — optimized to be human-readable and easily understood,
even by those unfamiliar with domain-specific terminology.

If not provided, the name should be used for display (except for Tool,
where `annotations.title` should be given precedence over using `name`,
if present).

TaskStatus.description: Represents the status of a task at a specific point in time.

message.description: An optional, human-readable message providing more details about the current status.

state.description: The current state of the task's lifecycle.

timestamp.description: An ISO 8601 datetime string indicating when this status was recorded.

Message.description: Represents a single message in the conversation between a user and an agent.

contextId.description: The context identifier for this message, used to group related interactions.

extensions.description: The URIs of extensions that are relevant to this message.

kind.description: The type of this object, used as a discriminator. Always 'message' for a Message.

messageId.description: A unique identifier for the message, typically a UUID, generated by the sender.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for extensions. The key is an extension-specific identifier.

parts.description:
An array of content parts that form the message body. A message can be
composed of multiple parts of different types (e.g., text and files).

referenceTaskIds.description: A list of other task IDs that this message references for additional context.

role.description: Identifies the sender of the message. `user` for the client, `agent` for the service.

taskId.description: The identifier of the task this message is part of. Can be omitted for the first message of a new task.

ToolAnnotations.description:
Additional properties describing a Tool to clients.

NOTE: all properties in ToolAnnotations are **hints**.
They are not guaranteed to provide a faithful description of
tool behavior (including descriptive properties like `title`).

Clients should never make tool use decisions based on ToolAnnotations
received from untrusted servers.

destructiveHint.description:
If true, the tool may perform destructive updates to its environment.
If false, the tool performs only additive updates.

(This property is meaningful only when `readOnlyHint == false`)

Default: true

idempotentHint.description:
If true, calling the tool repeatedly with the same arguments
will have no additional effect on the its environment.

(This property is meaningful only when `readOnlyHint == false`)

Default: false

openWorldHint.description:
If true, this tool may interact with an "open world" of external
entities. If false, the tool's domain of interaction is closed.
For example, the world of a web search tool is open, whereas that
of a memory tool is not.

Default: true

readOnlyHint.description:
If true, the tool does not modify its environment.

Default: false

title.description: A human-readable title for the tool.

Icon.description: An optionally-sized icon that can be displayed in a user interface.

mimeType.description:
Optional MIME type override if the source MIME type is missing or generic.
For example: `"image/png"`, `"image/jpeg"`, or `"image/svg+xml"`.

sizes.description:
Optional array of strings that specify sizes at which the icon can be used.
Each string should be in WxH format (e.g., `"48x48"`, `"96x96"`) or `"any"` for scalable formats like SVG.

If not provided, the client should assume that the icon can be used at any size.

src.description:
A standard URI pointing to an icon resource. May be an HTTP/HTTPS URL or a
`data:` URI with Base64-encoded image data.

Consumers SHOULD takes steps to ensure URLs serving icons are from the
same domain as the client/server or a trusted domain.

Consumers SHOULD take appropriate precautions when consuming SVGs as they can contain
executable JavaScript.

theme.description:
Optional specifier for the theme this icon is designed for. `light` indicates
the icon is designed to be used with a light background, and `dark` indicates
the icon is designed to be used with a dark background.

If not provided, the client should assume the icon can be used with any theme.

Annotations.description: Optional annotations for the client. The client can use annotations to inform how objects are used or displayed

audience.description:
Describes who the intended customer of this object or data is.

It can include multiple entries to indicate content useful for multiple audiences (e.g., `["user", "assistant"]`).

lastModified.description:
The moment the resource was last modified, as an ISO 8601 formatted string.

Should be an ISO 8601 formatted string (e.g., "2025-01-12T15:00:58Z").

Examples: last activity timestamp in an open file, timestamp when the resource
was attached, etc.

priority.description:
Describes how important this data is for operating the server.

A value of 1 means "most important," and indicates that the data is
effectively required, while 0 means "least important," and indicates that
the data is entirely optional.

OAuthFlows.description: Defines the configuration for the supported OAuth 2.0 flows.

authorizationCode.description: Configuration for the OAuth Authorization Code flow. Previously called accessCode in OpenAPI 2.0.

clientCredentials.description: Configuration for the OAuth Client Credentials flow. Previously called application in OpenAPI 2.0.

implicit.description: Configuration for the OAuth Implicit flow.

password.description: Configuration for the OAuth Resource Owner Password flow.

Part.description:
A discriminated union representing a part of a message or artifact, which can
be text, a file, or structured data.

model.description: The name of the model to use

reasoningEffort.description: Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. gtp-5.1 defaults to NONE, previous ones default to MEDIUM.

topLogprobs.description: Number of most likely tokens to return at each position

maxOutputTokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate

model.description: The name of the model to use

thinkingLevel.description: The level of thoughts tokens that the model should generate.

thinkingBudget.description: Indicates the thinking budget in tokens. 0 is DISABLED. -1 is AUTOMATIC. The default values and allowed ranges are model dependent.

temperature.description: Controls the degree of randomness in token selection. Lower temperatures are good for prompts that require a less open-ended or creative response, while higher temperatures can lead to more diverse or creative results.

topP.description: Tokens are selected from the most to least probable until the sum of their probabilities equals this value. Use a lower value for less random responses and a higher value for more random responses.

responseLogprobs.description: Whether to return the log probabilities of the tokens that were chosen by the model at each step

maxOutputTokens.description: Maximum number of tokens that can be generated in the response

Role.description: The sender or recipient of messages and data in a conversation.

PushNotificationConfig.description: Defines the configuration for setting up push notifications for task updates.

authentication.description: Optional authentication details for the agent to use when calling the notification URL.

id.description:
A unique ID for the push notification configuration, set by the client
to support multiple notification callbacks.

token.description: A unique token for this task or session to validate incoming push notifications.

url.description: The callback URL where the agent should send push notifications.

TaskState.description: Defines the lifecycle states of a Task.

ImplicitOAuthFlow.description: Defines configuration details for the OAuth 2.0 Implicit flow.

authorizationUrl.description: The authorization URL to be used for this flow. This MUST be a URL.

refreshUrl.description: The URL to be used for obtaining refresh tokens. This MUST be a URL.

scopes.description:
The available scopes for the OAuth2 security scheme. A map between the scope
name and a short description for it.

PasswordOAuthFlow.description: Defines configuration details for the OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password flow.

refreshUrl.description: The URL to be used for obtaining refresh tokens. This MUST be a URL.

scopes.description:
The available scopes for the OAuth2 security scheme. A map between the scope
name and a short description for it.

tokenUrl.description: The token URL to be used for this flow. This MUST be a URL.

AuthorizationCodeOAuthFlow.description: Defines configuration details for the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow.

authorizationUrl.description:
The authorization URL to be used for this flow.
This MUST be a URL and use TLS.

refreshUrl.description:
The URL to be used for obtaining refresh tokens.
This MUST be a URL and use TLS.

scopes.description:
The available scopes for the OAuth2 security scheme. A map between the scope
name and a short description for it.

tokenUrl.description:
The token URL to be used for this flow.
This MUST be a URL and use TLS.

TextPart.description: Represents a text segment within a message or artifact.

kind.description: The type of this part, used as a discriminator. Always 'text'.

metadata.description: Optional metadata associated with this part.

text.description: The string content of the text part.

ClientCredentialsOAuthFlow.description: Defines configuration details for the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow.

refreshUrl.description: The URL to be used for obtaining refresh tokens. This MUST be a URL.

scopes.description:
The available scopes for the OAuth2 security scheme. A map between the scope
name and a short description for it.

tokenUrl.description: The token URL to be used for this flow. This MUST be a URL.

DataPart.description: Represents a structured data segment (e.g., JSON) within a message or artifact.

kind.description: The type of this part, used as a discriminator. Always 'data'.

metadata.description: Optional metadata associated with this part.

FilePart.description:
Represents a file segment within a message or artifact. The file content can be
provided either directly as bytes or as a URI.

file.description: The file content, represented as either a URI or as base64-encoded bytes.

kind.description: The type of this part, used as a discriminator. Always 'file'.

metadata.description: Optional metadata associated with this part.

PushNotificationAuthenticationInfo.description: Defines authentication details for a push notification endpoint.

credentials.description: Optional credentials required by the push notification endpoint.

schemes.description: A list of supported authentication schemes (e.g., 'Basic', 'Bearer').

FileWithBytes.description: Represents a file with its content provided directly as a base64-encoded string.

bytes.description: The base64-encoded content of the file.

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the file (e.g., "application/pdf").

name.description: An optional name for the file (e.g., "document.pdf").

FileWithUri.description: Represents a file with its content located at a specific URI.

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the file (e.g., "application/pdf").

name.description: An optional name for the file (e.g., "document.pdf").

uri.description: A URL pointing to the file's content.
